title: fix(plugin-detail): fail closed when a related-list column has no resolvable identity
body:
Fixes #8793

`record:related_list`'s field-security fold kept any column entry whose identity
it could not resolve. That entry then rendered its real value through the table
library's own key. The else-branch now excludes it.

Arm A (fail closed) is the maintainer's ruling. This branch implements it; it
does not re-open the design question.

## ⭐ The measurement that dissolved this card's residual risk

The original body carried exactly one residual risk: *a host outside this
repository could pass the undeclared gate props AND author `accessorKey`
columns, and those columns would stop rendering.*

The protocol refuses that shape outright. Measured in the spec SOURCE on
`objectstack` `origin/main` `86c5052` — `@objectstack/spec` does not resolve
from a plain objectui checkout, which is how two earlier probes of this came
back dark:

```
packages/spec/src/ui/component.zod.ts:1091
  columns: z.array(z.string()).optional()
```

`record:related_list.columns` is declared as an ARRAY OF STRINGS. An object
entry — the `accessorKey` spelling included — is not authorable at this key at
all. `accessorKey` occurs exactly ONCE in the entire spec source and that
occurrence is a COMMENT (`src/conversions/registry.ts:7239`) describing
objectui's own read chain.

CONTROLS, lit in the same run so the one-hit reading is a reading and not a dark
probe: `RecordRelatedListProps` hits 3 files, `displayField` hits 17.

⇒ a host authoring that shape is authoring something the protocol rejects.
Failing closed on it is not a regression.

## The base moved, and it was merged in

`origin/main` was merged into this branch — never rebased, never force-pushed.
Merge-base was `2b10ca0f5`, with main 48 commits ahead of it.
`git merge-tree --write-tree` reported NO conflict at this base and the merge
applied clean, so the earlier "possible textual conflict" probe does not hold
here. Both adjacent repairs were verified intact at the source afterwards:

- objectui#9090's `redactFields` push-down survives in `record-related-list.tsx`,
  and its `filterRedacted` — resolving `accessorKey || columnIdentity(c)` —
  survives in `RelatedList.tsx`.
- This branch's `return n ? allowed.has(n) : false` survives in the same fold,
  fourteen lines above the push-down.
- objectui#9054's sibling repair in `record-details.tsx` is untouched.

## ⚠️ Re-measured on the merged head: this repair moves LESS than the original body claimed

Everything in the original body was measured at `fb1fb875b`, which predates
objectui#9090. Re-running this branch's own ablation at the merged head changed
the answer, and the honest version is smaller than the one it replaces.

Mutating the else-branch back to `true`:

```
before : 1 occurrence of ': false;', 0 of ': true;'
after  : 0 occurrences of ': false;', 1 of ': true;'   blob b66fe1f8 -> 17243d19
run    : 2 failed | 23 passed (25)
restore: 'git diff HEAD' empty AND blob back to b66fe1f8
```

At `fb1fb875b` three rendered-cell rows failed under that mutation. At the merged
head, ZERO of the original six do. objectui#9090 gave the redact leg a second
gate below this fold, and `RelatedList.filterFLS` has always been the second gate
for a DECLARED field that field security denies — both resolve the very
`accessorKey || columnIdentity` pair this fold refuses, so neither can see this
arm any more.

Rows that cannot fail are not evidence, so the test file was repaired rather than
inherited:

- **Added `THE RESIDUAL LEG`** — the one leg this arm still decides alone: a key
  the child object never DECLARES. `perms.checkField` default-ALLOWS it
  downstream, so the block's fold is the only gate and the fold cannot name it.
  Rendered over the real `RelatedList` and the real table, with the live control
  in the same render. It is one of the two rows that red under the mutation.
- **Re-pinned `THE LIMIT OF THIS REPAIR`** — it pinned objectui#9053 as the
  behaviour it then was and stated it would red when that landed. It landed and
  it did. The fall-through to auto-derived columns is unchanged and is still this
  repair's bound, so the row keeps pinning it — with `status`, a field never
  authored in that case, as the live control proving the derivation actually ran
  — and now also pins that the redacted value no longer comes back with it.

The second row that reds under the mutation is the member-level pin in
`RecordRelatedListRenderer.columnMembers.test.tsx`, which reads the array the
block hands down through a mocked `RelatedList`.

⛔ No assertion was weakened to make anything pass. Both rows that changed
changed what they SAY, and both remain able to fail.

## The objectui#9090 successor obligation, discharged

Three sites asserted that keeping an unnameable entry was a field-security
bypass, full stop. That was true when written and is now two-thirds true. All
three now state what the ablation measured:

- `apps/console/src/__tests__/registry-inputs-spec-parity.test.ts` — the
  `record:related_list.columns` member-pin prose. Its predecessor text predicted
  its own death ("this row reds when it lands"); the prediction has now been paid
  twice, once for objectui#9090's half and once for this branch's half.
- `RecordRelatedListRenderer.columnMembers.test.tsx` — the row's own comment.
- `packages/plugin-detail/src/renderers/record-related-list.tsx` — the comment at
  the fold.

## The defect

Two read points resolve a related-list column's identity and they disagree; the
security filter uses only one of them.

- The block's own fold resolves through `columnIdentity`, which deliberately
  refuses `accessorKey` (`TABLE_ADAPTER_COLUMN_KEY`, objectui#3104 — it is
  TanStack Table's column key, not ObjectStack metadata identity), plus a `key`
  tail fallback this block adds.
- `RelatedList` resolves a column as `accessorKey || columnIdentity(c)`, where
  `accessorKey` is first-class.

So a column authored in the `accessorKey` spelling was named by nobody in the
filter, took the `: true` arm, skipped both `enforceFieldSecurity` and
`redactFields` — and then painted its value through the table's own key.

## The repair

One site, one arm: the filter's else-branch now excludes rather than keeps. The
comment at the site records why, because the next reader will otherwise read a
`false` as timidity.

⛔ `columnIdentity` is **not** widened to accept `accessorKey` — objectui#3104
excluded it deliberately, and merging the table library's vocabulary into
metadata identity would leak the same confusion into all 20 of its importers.

## Blast radius — RE-RUN at the merged head, not inherited

Population: all 7414 tracked files (was 7328).

```bash
# 1. Who can even reach the fold? Every tracked occurrence of the two gate keys.
git grep -l "enforceFieldSecurity\|redactFields" -- .
# -> 18 files (was 11). Every addition is repo-internal: the landed
#    objectui#9053 / objectui#9054 tests and changesets, this branch's own files.
#    Still ZERO authored metadata, fixtures or docs; the only non-renderer
#    non-test hit remains apps/console/src/pages/shared-record-shape.ts, an
#    unrelated server-share wire key (verified again at the source).

# 2. Related lists and the accessorKey spelling in the same file.
git grep -l "record:related_list" -- . | sort > /tmp/rl.txt
git grep -l "accessorKey"        -- . | sort > /tmp/ak.txt
comm -12 /tmp/rl.txt /tmp/ak.txt
# -> 24 files (was 16): 10 CHANGELOG/changeset entries, 2 docs, 1 designer i18n
#    table, 1 console parity ledger, 7 test files, 3 renderer sources.
```

**POSITIVE CONTROL for command 2, and it PRE-DATES this branch** (it arrived on
main with objectui#7997 / PR 8984, so it cannot have been lit by anything here):
`packages/plugin-detail/src/__tests__/DetailView.relatedEntryRetired-7997.test.tsx:115`
really does author a related-list column in the `accessorKey` spelling. The
command finds the shape it is looking for.

**The verdict is unchanged and now stronger: ZERO columns in this repository stop
rendering.** No in-repo producer sets either gate key, so the fold never runs
outside tests at all: `deriveRelatedLists.ts` forwards `relatedListColumns`
(every in-repo instance is `['name','status']`), `buildDefaultPageSchema.ts`
forwards `rel.columns`, and the designer's block config for `record:related_list`
exposes only `objectName` / `relationshipField` / `title` / `limit`, so it cannot
author a column at all.

**Boundary of the sweep, stated**: it covers this repository, and the host case
outside it is the one the spec measurement above dissolves.

## The objectui#9053 hole is no longer open — objectui#9090 repaired it, not this branch

The original body reported a louder second hole: when the fold removed EVERY
authored member, `RelatedList` read the empty array as "no columns were authored"
and derived a replacement set that `redactFields` never reached, so a redacted
field came back. It was filed and it has since been repaired on main by
objectui#9090, which pushes `redactFields` down into the component that decides
columns. This branch's `THE LIMIT OF THIS REPAIR` row now pins that outcome
instead of the old one.

## Assumptions tested against the merged base

| # | Claim | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| A | `columnIdentity` excludes `accessorKey` per objectui#3104 | **Held.** Read at the source: `TABLE_ADAPTER_COLUMN_KEY`, docblock "NOT an identity key — deliberately excluded". |
| B | The `: true` arm is the only fail-open on this path | **Falsified** (original run). `record-details.tsx` carried the identical branch; repaired on main by objectui#9054, not here. `record-highlights.tsx` fails CLOSED already and is the contrast case. |
| C | `enforceFieldSecurity` / `redactFields` are the only two security functions on this path | **Falsified, twice over.** `RelatedList.filterFLS` was the third; since objectui#9090 `RelatedList.filterRedacted` is a fourth. Both read `accessorKey`, which is precisely why the measured reach of THIS arm shrank to the residual leg. |
| D | The card's path:line anchors are stale | **Held in effect.** Everything was re-derived by symbol; no line citation appears in the diff. |
| E | objectui#8882's tab badge does not share this filter | **Held.** `RelatedCountStore.fetch` has no column input at any point. |
| F | Closing the filter cannot render zero columns | **Held.** It renders the auto-derived set instead — and since objectui#9090 that set is redaction-filtered too, which is the row re-pinned above. |
| G | The PM's "possible textual conflict" probe | **Falsified at this base.** `git merge-tree --write-tree` exits 0 with a tree and the merge applied clean. |
| H | The PM's "merge-base is d2f0c10" | **Falsified, immaterially.** The merge-base is `2b10ca0f5`; `d2f0c10` is the shared checkout's HEAD. The conclusion — main had moved a long way — was right. |

## Tests

`RecordRelatedListRenderer.unresolvedIdentityFailClosed-8793.test.tsx` — seven
cases over the REAL `RelatedList` and the real `data-table`, reading rendered
cells: the reported leg, the three-row boundary, the FLS leg, the residual leg
(new, and the only rendered row that can fail for this change), the counter-probe
that bounds the change, the downstream-FLS census, and the re-pinned limit.

Every positive carries a LIVE CONTROL in the same render: a resolvable, allowed
column must still show its values. Without it, "the redacted value is gone" is
equally satisfied by a fold that filtered everything out.

The member-level pin in `RecordRelatedListRenderer.columnMembers.test.tsx` still
pins that the drop is by unresolvability rather than by matching the redacted
name, and that an unfiltered list hands the member down untouched.

## Verification, re-run at the merged head

```
pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-detail/     168 files, 1569 tests, all pass
pnpm exec vitest run apps/console/.../registry-inputs-spec-parity.test.ts  198 pass
@object-ui/plugin-detail type-check (tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json)  exit 0
   (both changed pins proven inside the typechecked set: --listFiles lists them)
@object-ui/console type-check                                             exit 0
turbo run build --filter='@object-ui/plugin-detail^...'   11/11 tasks successful
turbo run build --filter='@object-ui/console^...'         34/34 tasks successful
check:control-bytes, check:new-line-citations, check:vi-mock-specifiers,
check:vi-mock-inherit, check:vi-mock-override-shape, check:changeset-claims,
check:comment-mask-corpus, check:unreferenced-sources,
check-changeset-presence, check-changeset-no-major                        all exit 0
check-governed-queue-guard --test (the 5 changed paths)     NOT GOVERNED
```

The plugin-detail suite ran at `f57fb29c7`; its `packages/plugin-detail` tree
object is byte-identical to the one at the final commit (`6182da157` at both), and
the only change since is the console parity file, whose own suite was re-run green
on the bytes that were committed.

Lint is narrowed to the changed files and the narrowing is declared: the config's
own population is `**/*.{ts,tsx}` (4666 tracked files); this run linted 4 files
(count read from `--format json`), 0 errors, 41 pre-existing `no-explicit-any` and
`react-refresh` warnings; and `eslint.config.js` has no `parserOptions.project`
and no `projectService` (grep count 0 for each), so type-aware linting is off and
this diff cannot move the verdict on any untouched file. Measured at `9303d069a`.
The repo-wide run is CI's.

## Scope

The triage star — that both read points should end up agreeing — is correct and
out of scope; unifying them is a larger change than this branch. The two
successor cards this branch spawned, objectui#9053 and objectui#9054, have both
landed on main and are merged in here rather than re-implemented.

⚠️ This is a security boundary. The PR stays in **draft** and the maintainer
lands it; it was not flipped ready and no auto-merge was enabled.
